summary: Hardcoded author-controlled RabbitMQ broker routes installer events and delivers remote-invocation payloads
details: The package's bootstrapCore() calls initEventBus() with a hardcoded amqps:// URL (with embedded credentials) pointing at dog.lmq.cloudamqp.com, a CloudAMQP broker controlled by the package author. The URL is not sourced from caller options and cannot be overridden. Consequently, every event an installer publishes through this library is routed to the author's broker, and every message the broker returns is dispatched into the installer's own method handlers via instance[methodName](payload) — meaning the author (or anyone with credentials to that broker) can trigger arbitrary registered handlers in the installer's process with attacker-supplied payloads. Separately, ConfigurationService._defaultOptions.redisURL defaults to a hardcoded redis:// URL with credentials for a Redis Cloud instance under the author's account; consumers that do not explicitly pass redisURL will cache data (including values written by SecretManagerService.setKey) into the author's Redis. The tarball additionally embeds five cleartext RSA private keys — a GCP Secret Manager service-account key for project for-poc-325210 and four Firebase Admin SDK service-account keys (for-poc-325210 super, for-poc-325210 user, lyxa-rider-88939, lyxa-shop) — as well as credentialed URLs for the CloudAMQP and Redis Cloud instances; those credentials authorize access to the author's own backends and do not by themselves compromise the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
